name: Do I need to replace the shower valve inside the wall when updating my shower trim?

mainEntity.name: Do I need to replace the shower valve inside the wall when updating my shower trim?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, existing shower valves usually must be replaced when switching to a different trim brand or updated valve system. Shower trim plates and handles attach directly to the rough-in valve body soldered behind the shower wall. Because valve designs vary significantly by manufacturer and manufacturing year, you cannot install a new brand's trim kit onto an older or mismatched valve. Replacing the valve requires accessing the wall cavity, which is best completed during a shower tile renovation.
acceptedAnswer.description: Usually yes. Shower trim is specific to the manufacturer and valve model, meaning a new brand or modernized setup typically requires replacing the concealed rough-in valve.
